C9 note
C9 · The ledger, one toggle away
The two-sided ledger still exists for the moments Maya wants to see raw lines: the Inbox / Ledger toggle keeps the same difference and 14-segment bar, filtered to the 26 open lines.
Every line carries its thread chip (Ember confidence, message count), so the ledger is an index into conversations rather than a separate workflow.
Here she pairs the Gusto contractors herself: ⌘-click L CHEN on the bank side and Lin Chen in books, the bar checks Δ and payee, and M posts the match into the Gusto thread (row order would have paired them wrong).
Trade-off: two surfaces to keep in sync. Worth testing whether Maya ever needs this once she trusts the cards.

C1 note
C1 · The rec is an inbox
Maya lands on 14 threads, not 219 lines. Each row is one exception plus Ember’s one-line proposal and confidence, already split into Ready to accept / Needs a look / Needs approval, so triage is done before she reads anything.
The list header carries the two numbers that matter: open threads (14 → 0, with a 14-segment bar) and the live difference.
The right pane is the thread. Ember’s proposal is the first message: a structured card with the real bank and book lines, the entry it will post, and Accept / Reject. Priya’s note and Ember’s audit-log check sit under it, so the context lives next to the decision. Evidence renders inline.
Unread dots mark threads where a person said something. That is where Maya starts.
Trade-off: the two-sided ledger is one click away (Ledger toggle), not on screen. The bet is that the lines inside each card are enough to decide.

C2 note
C2 · Why, inline
Google is 93%, but GSUITE_ARBORANA vs Google Workspace is only 41% similar, so Maya presses W. The formula opens inside the card: five factors, weight × score each, summing to 93. Payee is weak; alias history carries it. She can see that in one glance.
A accepts and jumps to the next open thread (Superhuman’s archive-and-next). The toast confirms the previous one with Undo (U), so moving fast stays safe.
Note the difference reads $32.02 with 9 open. It swings as items resolve (the $86,400 deposit in transit alone moves it), so the thread count is the progress signal and the difference is the final proof. Worth testing whether Maya reads a near-zero difference as “almost done”.

C3 note
C3 · Talk it through
Notion is 72% with no bill in AP. Instead of hunting, Maya asks in the thread. Ember’s tool calls show as steps (what it searched, what it read), and every data change it made is its own row with Revert: it added an option (unprocessed invoice NTN-88213, 96%) and dropped one it now thinks is wrong.
The superseded proposal collapses to one line; the new card is what she acts on.
She @mentions Priya in the same thread to fix the root cause (the AP inbox). The whole exchange — question, tool calls, evidence, human decision — is the training trace Campfire wants.
Trade-off: conversation is slower than a click. It is for the 3–4 threads that need it, not the default path.
